note: Discovery web for milestone 1. Each tile is a family of stages; each stage has its own needs, effects, and optional accident situation. Refs point at stage ids (tile.stage). 'any': true means any one ref is enough.

tiles.name: Fire
tiles.sum: Modern humans arrive able to make and keep fire. Mastery grows from there.

stages.name: Making and keeping fire
stages.does: Warmth, light, cooking, keeps predators back.

stages.name: Built hearths

needs.text: staying two weeks or more in one spot
flat stones to ring the fire

stages.does: Steady cooking heat; a place people gather and talk.

stages.name: High-heat fires

needs.text: dense hardwood or plenty of fuel
a job that needs real heat: hardening wood, treating flint
interested in fire, practiced at tending it

stages.does: Hot enough to fire clay and heat-treat flint.
stages.accident: A hearth dug into a sheltered pit runs far hotter than usual.

stages.name: Burning the land

needs.text: grazing herds that come back for fresh shoots

stages.does: Burned clearings draw game and help wild grain grow.
stages.accident: After a wildfire (natural, or your lightning), herds return to the green shoots.

stages.name: Torches

needs.text: dark places or night: deep caves, predators at night

stages.does: Light to carry: deep caves, night watches, scaring predators.
stages.accident: A resin-soaked branch pulled from the fire burns long and bright.

stages.name: Stone fat lamps

needs.text: torches and pounding (to hollow a stone)

stages.does: Steady light deep inside caves and shelters.

tiles.name: Knapping
tiles.sum: Shaping stone into edges. Skill level matters for everything downstream.

stages.name: Flakes and scrapers
stages.does: Cutting, scraping hides, carving wood.

stages.name: Long blades
stages.does: Better knives; blanks for points and awls.

stages.name: Hafted points

needs.text: sinew thread, plant twine, or tree resin

stages.does: Stone points fixed to shafts: spears, later arrows.

stages.name: Heat-treated flint
stages.does: Flint flakes cleaner; finer, sharper points.
stages.accident: Flint left in the hearth overnight flakes far better the next day.

tiles.name: Bone & antler
tiles.sum: Butchering leaves bone and antler: tough, carvable material for points, needles and hooks.

stages.name: Bone awls and points

needs.text: long blades to cut and scrape it

stages.does: Piercing hides; simple points.
stages.accident: A splinter of split bone turns out sharper and tougher than expected.

stages.name: Bone and antler spear points
stages.does: Spear and arrow points where flint is scarce.

stages.name: Eyed needles

needs.text: clothes that need fine, tight seams

stages.does: Fine sewing: fitted clothes and footwear.

stages.name: Bone fish hooks

needs.text: fish in water too deep to spear

stages.does: Hook-and-line fishing.

stages.name: Barbed harpoons
stages.does: Large fish and seals; coastal life becomes rich.

tiles.name: Woodworking
tiles.sum: From whittling spears to felling trees and hollowing boats.

stages.name: Shaping wood with stone
stages.does: Spears, digging sticks, handles.

stages.name: Hafted stone axes

needs.text: need for big timber or firewood: shelters, long winters

stages.does: Felling small trees; poles and timber.

stages.name: Ground and polished axes
stages.does: Axes that do not shatter. Big trees come down.

stages.name: Dugout canoes

needs.text: polished axes and high-heat fires (burn and scrape)
a big straight tree, water to travel
food or people across the water

stages.does: Real boats. Crossing to other islands starts here.

tiles.name: Spear
tiles.sum: Hunting and defense. Armed adults also keep wolves at a distance.

stages.name: Fire-hardened wooden spear
stages.does: Thrusting and short throws; counts toward band strength.

stages.name: Stone-tipped spear
stages.does: Bigger game; more band strength.

stages.name: Light throwing spears

needs.text: fast prey that won't let hunters close

stages.does: Longer throws; the base for the spear-thrower.

tiles.name: Trapping
tiles.sum: Catching animals while you sleep. Patient hunters and children often find it first.

stages.name: Reading game trails
stages.does: Knowing exactly where small animals pass.

stages.name: Snares

needs.text: hunters away, small game around camp

stages.does: Rabbits and birds caught without anyone there.
stages.accident: An animal tangles itself in a loop of cord left on a trail.

stages.name: Deadfalls and pits

needs.text: larger game or predators near camp

stages.does: Bigger catches; predator control adds band strength.
stages.accident: A rockfall pins an animal on a trail.

stages.name: Spring-pole snares
stages.does: Snares that lift the catch out of reach. The stored-energy idea behind the bow.

tiles.name: Foraging
tiles.sum: Knowing which plants feed you, where and when.

stages.name: Patches and seasonal rounds
stages.does: The band moves through the year to where food is.

stages.name: Plant lore

needs.text: shared stories, so lore outlives one person
interested in plants; elders still alive to teach

stages.does: Medicines (fewer deaths), poisons, knowing which plants make good fiber.

stages.name: Leaching nuts and acorns

needs.text: oaks or nut trees, running water

stages.does: Bitter nuts become a big, storable food.
stages.accident: Acorns dropped in a stream lose their bitterness.

tiles.name: Language
tiles.sum: Full spoken language from day one. Its stages decide how far and how faithfully knowledge and beliefs travel.

stages.name: Everyday speech and teaching
stages.does: Skills taught by showing plus words; every discovery adds new words.

stages.name: Shared stories

needs.text: a remembered event retold by several people: a great hunt, a disaster, an omen
long evenings together, such as winters around the fire

stages.does: Beliefs and lessons outlive the people who lived them; less drift between generations. Myths about you start here.

stages.name: Ritual speech and song

needs.text: rites for the dead, or a belief built on omens

stages.does: Rituals hit harder; belief strength and group cohesion rise.

stages.name: Counting and tally marks

needs.text: keeping track of stores or of moons until a season

stages.does: Tracking seasons and stores; helps grain timing; groundwork for trade later.

tiles.name: Cordage
tiles.sum: Two routes in. Sinew cultures sew and string bows; plant cultures fish, build and net. Both opens everything.

stages.name: Sinew thread

needs.text: things that need binding: hafting, mending

stages.does: Sewing, strong bowstrings, tight lashings.
stages.accident: Wet sinew wrapped around a cracked handle dries rock-hard.

stages.name: Plant twine

needs.text: big foraging hauls to carry and tie

stages.does: Basket lashing, fishing lines, long cords.
stages.accident: Stems absently twisted during a rest hold together under pull.

stages.name: Two-ply string
stages.does: Stronger everything: bowstrings, hafting, lines.

stages.name: Rope

needs.text: two-ply string, made from plants (sinew is too short)

stages.does: Lashing shelters, hauling, rafts later.

stages.name: Knotted nets

needs.text: water to fish, or loads to carry

stages.does: Fishing nets and carrying nets.

tiles.name: Cooking
tiles.sum: Cooking gets more food out of the same harvest, makes meat safe, and makes soft food that the very young and old can live on.

stages.name: Roasting
stages.does: Meat, roots and nuts give more food; cooked meat rarely makes people sick.

stages.name: Hot-stone cooking
stages.does: Even, thorough cooking; more food from everything.
stages.accident: A stone left in the fire scalds whatever is set on it, and the food comes out better.

stages.name: Boiling

needs.text: a scraped hide or a pitch-sealed basket to hold water

stages.does: Soups and mush: toddlers wean onto soft food, elders eat well, starchy food gives much more.
stages.accident: A hot stone dropped into a water-filled hide makes it boil.

stages.name: Bone grease
stages.does: Rich fat that keeps, from bones that were thrown away. A real winter lifeline.

stages.name: Earth ovens
stages.does: Big batches; tough roots become good food.

stages.name: Flatbread
stages.does: Grain becomes a staple.

stages.name: Pot cooking
stages.does: Stews and porridge: all of the above, easily.

tiles.name: Drying & smoking
tiles.sum: Making food last into the lean season. Usually starts by accident.

stages.name: Food that keeps

needs.text: more meat, fish or berries than can be eaten

stages.does: Food lasts days instead of hours.
stages.accident: Meat left hanging in the smoke is still good a week later. The main way in.

stages.name: Drying racks

needs.text: a built hearth, or steady sun
a hard winter after a good autumn

stages.does: Preserve a whole kill or harvest; real stores become possible.

stages.name: Smoking

needs.text: a surplus of fish or meat

stages.does: Food lasts months. A fish run can now feed a winter.

stages.name: Pemmican
stages.does: Dried meat pounded with fat: keeps longest and packs the most food.

tiles.name: Spear-thrower
tiles.sum: A hooked stick that throws a spear much farther. One road to the bow.

stages.name: Hooked throwing stick
stages.does: Kills at range; more band strength.

stages.name: Fletched darts
stages.does: Accurate darts. The idea of fletching carries over to arrows.

tiles.name: Grinding stones
tiles.sum: Turning hard seeds and nuts into food. The heavier stages need a band that stays put.

stages.name: Pounding

needs.text: a hammerstone plus nuts or seeds
plenty of starchy food that's hard to eat whole

stages.does: Nuts and seeds become food.
stages.accident: Nuts cracked on the same rock for weeks leave a smooth hollow.

stages.name: Mortar and pestle
stages.does: Faster, finer meal.

stages.name: Grinding slab

needs.text: a big flat stone (too heavy to carry) and wild grain

stages.does: Flour. Wild grain becomes worth the effort.

tiles.name: Dog companions
tiles.sum: Wolves become dogs over generations, but only if the band is strong enough that wolves lurk instead of attack.

stages.name: Wolves at the edge of camp

needs.text: band strength high enough that wolves stay back: armed adults, fire

stages.does: Not a discovery, a situation. Wolves scavenge and their howls warn of other predators.

stages.name: A pup raised in camp

needs.text: wolves at the edge of camp

stages.does: One tame wolf. Its pups are tamer.
stages.accident: An orphaned pup is found after its mother is killed. The main way in.

stages.name: Camp dogs

needs.text: several generations of the tamest pups kept

stages.does: Guarding (more band strength), cleaning scraps, warmth.

stages.name: Hunting dogs

needs.text: skilled hunter who works with them

stages.does: Tracking and cornering prey. Hunts succeed far more often.

tiles.name: Burial & rites
tiles.sum: The first culture tile. Ties people to a place and creates the ritual specialist.

stages.name: Covering the dead

needs.text: the death of someone loved or respected

stages.does: Graves become places that matter.

stages.name: Grave goods

needs.text: the dead go on somewhere, or are linked to the sky one

stages.does: Objects take on meaning beyond use.

stages.name: Ancestor rites
stages.does: A ritual specialist emerges. Strong attachment to place.

tiles.name: Ochre & art
tiles.sum: Art as belief made visible. Cave walls come from the Synty Alpine caves.

stages.name: Body paint

needs.text: a ritual, a status, or a need to mark who 'we' are
interested in spirits, sky or people

stages.does: Group identity; ritual looks the part.
stages.accident: Someone notices the red stain ochre leaves on their hands.

stages.name: Handprints and marks

needs.text: a cave or sheltered rock wall

stages.does: Places get claimed and remembered.

stages.name: Cave paintings

needs.text: interested in spirits or animals, skilled hands
torches or lamps to work deep inside

stages.does: Beliefs become very stable. Hunting magic beliefs form.

stages.name: Carved and fired figures

needs.text: soft stone, bone or ivory; or clay that has been fired

stages.does: Portable sacred objects. The fired-clay version is real: figurines came 10,000 years before pots.

tiles.name: Basketry
tiles.sum: Carrying and holding more than hands can.

stages.name: Bundled reed carriers

needs.text: gathering more than hands can carry

stages.does: Bigger foraging hauls.

stages.name: Woven baskets
stages.does: Durable carriers; fish traps become possible.

stages.name: Tight baskets that hold seed
stages.does: Seed harvests and basket stores.

stages.name: Pitch-sealed baskets
stages.does: Carry water; boil food with hot stones.

tiles.name: Hide & sewing
tiles.sum: From wrapped skins to fitted clothes. Fitted clothing opens colder ground.

stages.name: Wrapped hides
stages.does: Basic warmth.

stages.name: Scraped and dried hides
stages.does: Hides last; covers for shelters.

stages.name: Stitched with an awl
stages.does: Bags, simple garments, joined shelter covers.

stages.name: Hide tents
stages.does: Real shelter; long stays get easier.

stages.name: Fitted clothing
stages.does: Big cold tolerance. Harsh lands become livable. Fitted boots too.

stages.name: Footwear

needs.text: cold, rough or thorny ground; long walks

stages.does: Faster, safer travel; fewer injuries and frostbite.

stages.name: Snowshoes
stages.does: Winter travel at normal speed; animals floundering in deep snow become easier to run down.

tiles.name: Shelter
tiles.sum: Where people sleep shapes how long they stay, and how they get sick.

stages.name: Windbreaks and brush shelters
stages.does: A night out of the wind.

stages.name: Caves and rock shelters

needs.text: fire, to drive out animals and keep warm
band strong enough to take it from bears or wolves

stages.does: Warm, defensible winter quarters; walls for art.
stages.accident: A storm drives the band into an overhang, and it stays dry all night.

stages.name: Lean-tos
stages.does: Quick, sturdier camp shelters.

stages.name: Pole-and-thatch huts
stages.does: Lasting homes; a camp starts to look like a place.

stages.name: Pit houses
stages.does: Half-buried, earth-covered houses. Warm all winter.

tiles.name: Fishing
tiles.sum: Turning a river into a reliable larder. People start out catching fish by hand; weirs and nets make the spring and autumn runs into gluts worth drying.

stages.name: Catching fish by hand
stages.does: Fish stranded in pools, groped from under banks, and shellfish: a little food from the water, unreliably.

stages.name: Spear fishing

needs.text: spear and catching fish by hand
a river or lake with fish

stages.does: More fish, from deeper water.
stages.accident: Fish trapped in a shrinking pool are caught by hand.

stages.name: Stake weirs

needs.text: stakes and a seasonal fish run

stages.does: Big catches during runs.

stages.name: Basket traps
stages.does: Steady catch with little work.

stages.name: Hook and line
stages.does: Fishing deep water.

stages.name: Nets
stages.does: The biggest, most reliable catches.

tiles.name: Bow & arrow
tiles.sum: Killing at range without being seen.

stages.name: Simple bow

needs.text: fast prey, or conflict with neighbors
spring-pole snares: the idea of stored spring

stages.does: Range and stealth; more band strength.
stages.accident: A spring-pole snare snaps back and flings its trigger stick across the trail.

stages.name: Fletched arrows

needs.text: simple bow (fletched darts help a lot)

stages.does: Accuracy.

stages.name: Stone-tipped arrows
stages.does: Lethal against big game.

stages.name: Sinew-backed bow

needs.text: simple bow, sinew thread and plant twine

stages.does: Much stronger bows.

tiles.name: Storage
tiles.sum: Changes how a band thinks about the future. Things worth guarding appear.

stages.name: Caches under stones
stages.does: A small buffer against hunger.
stages.accident: Food hidden from wolves is found intact weeks later.

stages.name: Lined pits
stages.does: Winter stores.

stages.name: Basket stores
stages.does: Seed and nut stores.

stages.name: Raised caches
stages.does: Stores safe from animals. Big enough to be worth stealing.

stages.name: Cold caches

needs.text: long freezing winters and meat to keep

stages.does: Meat buried in snow or frozen ground keeps all winter.
stages.accident: Meat left in a snowbank is still good weeks later.

tiles.name: Base camp
tiles.sum: Not a tool: a band choosing to mostly stay put. Unlocks heavy, fragile things, and new problems like disease.

stages.name: Seasonal return

needs.text: a place with dependable seasonal food
attachment to place; graves nearby help

stages.does: The same camp every year; things can be left behind.

stages.name: Long stays

needs.text: one reliable local food: weirs, nuts, or wild grain
moving costs more than staying: many children or elders, heavy stores

stages.does: Most of the year in one place. Heavy tools make sense.

stages.name: Year-round base

needs.text: hide tents, huts or pit houses

stages.does: Population grows; disease risk grows; the next milestone's villages start here.

tiles.name: Pottery
tiles.sum: The showcase of this milestone. Fired clay can happen early by accident, but pots need everything else to line up.

stages.name: Fired clay
stages.does: The insight that fire hardens clay. Figurines possible.
stages.accident: Clay pressed or dropped near a hearth comes out hard. The main way in.

stages.name: Pinch pots

needs.text: long stays (pots are too heavy for nomads)
a need to cook or hold liquids
curious, interested in fire or stone

stages.does: Small vessels.

stages.name: Coiled pots
stages.does: Real cooking pots: stews and porridge (grain becomes much more useful); sealed storage.

stages.name: Pit firing
stages.does: Reliable, sturdy pots. Kilns are next milestone.

tiles.name: Tending wild grain
tiles.sum: The doorway to farming, which is the next milestone.

stages.name: Harvesting wild stands

needs.text: something to hold seed: tight baskets

stages.does: A seasonal grain haul.

stages.name: Clearing competitors

needs.text: seasonal return, or burning the land

stages.does: Bigger wild stands near camp.

stages.name: Scattering seed nearby
stages.does: Grain grows where you want it.
stages.accident: Seed spilled on the camp's rubbish heap sprouts the next spring.

stages.name: Keeping the best seed

needs.text: tally marks for timing the seasons

stages.does: Seeds get bigger each generation. Farming begins next milestone.

tiles.name: Wayfinding
tiles.sum: Knowing the land: where food grows in each season, where game goes, where other people camp. Everyone carries a map in their head; naming places, drawing them and carrying them let people hold more, share more, and talk of farther places.

stages.name: Knowing the land by heart
stages.does: Each person remembers places they've seen or been told of; it fades for places long unvisited.

stages.name: Named places and routes

needs.text: wide ranges, many places to keep track of
sociable, a good memory for the land

stages.does: People hold twice as many places in mind and pass on more of them in talk.

stages.name: Ground maps

needs.text: planning a move, a hunt or a visit far away

stages.does: Lines in the dirt show others where things are: far places can be described, and much more is shared at once.
stages.accident: A stick idly traces the river's bend while someone explains where the herd crossed.

stages.name: Carried maps
stages.does: Maps on hide or bark keep what's known beyond any one memory.

stages.name: Star paths
stages.does: Finding the way by stars and landmarks: long journeys, and later the sea.

tiles.name: Hunting tactics
tiles.sum: How a party closes in on its quarry. Each band develops its own habits from what has worked for it, animal by animal.

stages.name: Stalking
stages.does: Creep within reach before the animals bolt. Hard with thrusting spears, easy with weapons that reach far.

stages.name: Waiting at water
stages.does: Wait where animals come to drink; slow, and rewards patience.

stages.name: Driving into wet ground
stages.does: Push a herd into marsh or river where it flounders; needs several people.

stages.name: Surrounding

needs.text: a skilled hunter who leads well

stages.does: A big party rings a herd in open ground and closes the circle.

stages.name: Running down

needs.text: hot days, prey that can't be approached

stages.does: Chase an animal through the heat of the day until it can run no more.
